the identification of cis‐acting regulatory elements in the mcb promoter and their role in controlling transcription.
the identification and characterization of regulatory elements in P mcb, the promoter of the m cb operon, which encodes proteins required for the biosynthesis of the cell surface lipopolysaccharide.
the identification of the cis‐acting sequences and trans‐acting factors required for mcb expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pmcb has at least four different regulatory elements, two of which are known and two unknown, acting at at least five different sites in the Pmcb region.
the mcb operone is regulated by at least three factors, OmpR, EmrR and a third unknown factor.
the Pmcb promoter contains at least four different sites, each of which is required for wild‐ type levels of mcb operon expression in both exponential and post‐exponential phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pmcb contains four distinct regulatory regions, each with a unique regulatory factor, that act at four different points within the Pmcb promoter.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Pmcb has a very complex promoter structure.
a number of different factors are required for the regulation of Pmcb and that the Pmcb promoter is not a simple model for stationary phase regulation.
